Below is a **minimal, self‑contained example** that shows how to: 1. Install the `vizdoom` package (the Python wrapper for the Doom engine). 2. Download the Doom binary that `vizdoom` needs. 3. Load a built‑in scenario (`basic.cfg`). 4. Run a *random* agent for a few episodes. > **Why a random agent?** > Training a good Doom agent (e.g. a DQN or PPO) takes hours/days on a GPU. > The code below is meant to be a quick “hello world” that lets you see the > environment working. > Once you’re comfortable, you can replace the random policy with a neural > network or use one of the official ViZDoom training scripts. --- ## 1. Install ViZDoom ```bash pip install vizdoom ``` > **Tip:** If you’re on Windows, you’ll also need the Visual C++ Redistributable > (it’s usually already present on recent Windows versions). --- ## 2. Download the Doom binary ViZDoom ships with a small “Doom binary” that contains the game logic. Download it from the official repo: ```bash # Linux/macOS wget https://github.com/mwydmuch/vizdoom/releases/download/v4.7.0/doom.wad -O doom.wad # Windows curl -L https://github.com/mwydmuch/vizdoom/releases/download/v4.7.0/doom.wad -o doom.wad ``` > **Where does ViZDoom look for it?** > By default it looks in the current working directory. > If you want to keep it elsewhere, set the environment variable `VIZDOOM_PATH` > to the folder that contains `doom.wad`. --- ## 3. Minimal Python script ```python import random import os from vizdoom import DoomGame, Mode, ScreenResolution, ActionSet def main(): # ------------------------------------------------------------------ # 1️⃣ Create the game instance # ------------------------------------------------------------------ game = DoomGame() game.set_doom_scenario_path("basic.cfg") # built‑in scenario game.set_doom_executable_path("doom.wad") # the binary we just downloaded game.set_screen_resolution(ScreenResolution.RES_640X480) game.set_mode(Mode.PLAYER) # single‑player mode game.set_window_visible(True) # show the window game.set_render_hud(False) # hide HUD for clarity game.set_render_minimal_viewport(False) # ------------------------------------------------------------------ # 2️⃣ Define the action set # ------------------------------------------------------------------ # The built‑in basic.cfg supports 3 actions: move forward, turn left, turn right # We’ll use a simple discrete action set that maps to those commands. action_set = ActionSet() action_set.add_action("move_forward") action_set.add_action("turn_left") action_set.add_action("turn_right") game.set_available_actions(action_set.get_actions()) # ------------------------------------------------------------------ # 3️⃣ Initialize the game # ------------------------------------------------------------------ game.init() # ------------------------------------------------------------------ # 4️⃣ Play a few episodes # ------------------------------------------------------------------ num_episodes = 3 max_steps_per_episode = 200 for episode in range(num_episodes): game.new_episode() print(f"\n=== Episode {episode + 1} ===") for step in range(max_steps_per_episode): # Get the current state (image + other info) state = game.get_state() if state is None: break # no more states (game over) # Render the screen (optional) # game.render() # uncomment if you want to see the window update each step # Randomly pick an action action = [0] * game.get_available_actions_size() action[random.randint(0, len(action) - 1)] = 1 # Execute the action reward = game.make_action(action) # Print some diagnostics print(f"Step {step + 1}: Reward={reward:.2f}") # Break if the episode is finished if game.is_episode_finished(): break # Episode finished – print the total reward print(f"Episode finished! Total reward: {game.get_total_reward():.2f}") # ------------------------------------------------------------------ # 5️⃣ Clean up # ------------------------------------------------------------------ game.close() if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ### What this script does | Step | What happens | |------|--------------| | 1 | Creates a `DoomGame` instance and points it at the built‑in `basic.cfg`. | | 2 | Sets up a very small action set (forward, left, right). | | 3 | Initializes the game (loads the binary, parses the scenario). | | 4 | Runs 3 episodes, each up to 200 steps. At each step it:
• grabs the current state
• chooses a random action
• executes it
• prints the reward | | 5 | Closes the game cleanly. | --- ## 4. Running the script ```bash python doom_random_agent.py ``` You should see a window pop up (if you kept `set_window_visible(True)`), and the console will print rewards for each step. The agent will die quickly because it’s random, but you’ll see the total reward printed at the end of each episode. --- ## 5. Going further Once you’re comfortable with the API, you can: 1. **Replace the random policy** with a neural network (e.g. a CNN that processes the screen image). 2. **Use the official ViZDoom training scripts** (they come with DQN, PPO, etc.). ```bash git clone https://github.com/mwydmuch/vizdoom.git cd vizdoom python -m vizdoom.train_dqn --scenario basic.cfg ``` 3. **Experiment with different scenarios** (`basic.cfg`, `basic_2d.cfg`, `basic_3d.cfg`, etc.). 4. **Add more actions** (shoot, jump, crouch) by editing the scenario file or using the `ActionSet` API. --- ## 6. Quick reference – ViZDoom API | Function / Method | Purpose | |-------------------|---------| | `game.set_doom_scenario_path(path)` | Path to a `.cfg` scenario file. | | `game.set_doom_executable_path(path)` | Path to the Doom binary (`doom.wad`). | | `game.set_screen_resolution(res)` | Resolution of the rendered screen. | | `game.set_mode(mode)` | `Mode.PLAYER` for single‑player. | | `game.set_available_actions(actions)` | List of actions the agent can take. | | `game.init()` | Load everything and start the game. | | `game.new_episode()` | Start a new episode. | | `game.get_state()` | Current state (image + other info). | | `game.make_action(action)` | Execute an action; returns the reward. | | `game.is_episode_finished()` | Check if the episode ended. | | `game.get_total_reward()` | Total reward accumulated in the episode. | | `game.close()` | Cleanly shut down the game. | --- ### TL;DR 1. Install `vizdoom`. 2. Download `doom.wad`. 3. Run the script above. 4. Replace the random policy with a neural net or use the official training scripts to get a real Doom agent. Happy hacking!
